newsitem.title: USA: FTC probes Philip Morris merchandising.
newsitem.headline: FTC probes Philip Morris merchandising.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission has launched an investigation into alleged restrictive merchandising practices at Philip Morris Cos Inc, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing made Wednesday.

In its 10Q filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in Washington, the company said the FTC's investigation was intended to determine whether the tobacco giant "unfairly restricts the distribution of competing manufacturers cigarette brands through its merchandising practices at the wholesale and retail level."
The company was not immediately available to comment on the investigation and further details were also not available.
In the SEC filing, the company said it "believes it has acted lawfully."
The trade commission investigation is one more headache for Philip Morris, the world's largest cigarette maker.

In the past two years, the domestic business environment for tobacco companies has disintegrated into one marked by a welter of state and private class-action lawsuits, personal injury suits, grand jury probes and the inception of federal regulatory oversight by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
